foundation.q: A bag has 9 sweets. How many sweets are in 7 bags?
foundation.work: Check recall of 9 x 7; note if the child skip-counts slowly.
Does the child multiply top and bottom by 4? Common error: 2 + 9 = 11.

foundation.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 6 cm wide. What is its area? Write your answer with units.
foundation.work: Accept 42 square cm, 42 sq cm or 42 cm2. If the unit is missing, give the mark and note it. Common error: giving the perimeter, 26 cm.
Watch for borrowing across zeros; common error 4346 or 3764.

core.q: A factor of 18 is a number that divides 18 exactly with nothing left over. Write down all the factors of 18.
core.work: Look for pairs (1 x 18, 2 x 9, 3 x 6). Common errors: missing 1 or 18, or listing multiples (18, 36...).
Check which digit they look at (the hundreds digit, 5). Common error: 48,000 or 48,600.
Multiplication first: 6 x 3 = 18, then 12 + 18 - 4. Common error: 50 (left to right).

core.q: 2 and 3/5 + 1 and 4/5 = ? Write your answer as a mixed number.
core.work: Mixed number preferred: 4 2/5. Accept 22/5 for the mark. Look for 3/5 + 4/5 = 7/5 = 1 2/5, then add the whole numbers. Common errors: 3 7/5 left unconverted, or 4 7/10.

core.q: A ribbon is 3.7 m long. Another ribbon is 2.85 m long. What is the total length? Write your answer in metres.
core.work: Check place-value alignment of the decimal points. Common errors: 3.22 (37 + 285 with the decimal point ignored) or 5.92 (digits lined up from the right).

core.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. It is 11 cm long. How wide is it?
core.work: Look for 36 / 2 = 18, then 18 - 11 = 7. Common errors: 25 (36 - 11) or 14.

stretch.q: (Brain stretchers are hard on purpose. Most children do not finish both, and that is fine. Try one!)  I am a number between 30 and 50. I am a multiple of 4 and a multiple of 6. My digits add up to 9. What number am I?
stretch.work: Look for listing multiples of 4 and 6 (common: 36, 48) then using the digit clue. Accept guess and check with reasoning.

stretch.q: Ben has 3 times as many marbles as Cara. Ben gives 12 marbles to Cara. Now they have the same number. How many marbles did Ben have at first?
stretch.work: Bar model: after the gift, Ben's 3 units minus 12 equals Cara's 1 unit plus 12, so 2 units = 24, 1 unit = 12. Cara 12, Ben 36.

topics: This check samples number, fractions, decimals, area and perimeter only. Angles, symmetry, nets and graphs are not in it.

placement.timeLine: Allow up to 40 minutes; stop when your child is tired.
placement.notTaughtTick: This has not been taught yet.
placement.notTaughtRule: If 2 or more main questions are ticked, chat with the tutor before the score is used.
placement.keyNote: Please do not mark in front of your child.
placement.lowerMarkBox: A lower mark tells us where to start, not what your child can do.

rows.6to8: Join {AGE} ({LV}). Your child has the foundations and will be well challenged.
rows.4or5: Join {AGE} ({LV}), and expect some support in the first weeks. If the warm-up score is 2 or less, {down} may be a happier start; ask us for a free 10-minute chat.
rows.0to3: {down} is likely to be the happier start. Ask us for a free 10-minute chat first. Starting where the ideas feel comfortable is how children get faster later. The age shown for {down} is a guide only: older children are welcome.

placement.greyZone: For a main + stretch score of 3 to 5, or a warm-up score of 2, offer a free 10-minute chat with the tutor before the child decides.
placement.swapRule: Free swap between levels up to the end of Lesson 2.
placement.tryUp: Try-up check: 4 questions from next year. It is normal to find these new.
